title: IMPRESS-A: the API and the loop

acts.name: Functionality
acts.question: what can you write against this that you cannot write against a pipeline?
acts.gap: every toolkit that exists is one of the four real stages of a single chain, plus mocks, and nobody outside this package has authored either a toolkit or a policy

acts.name: Performance
acts.question: what does the loop cost, and where does it serialise?
acts.gap: no concurrent run and no serial baseline anywhere in the deck, so nothing divides into a speedup - and the stages were mocks, so this times the ENGINE and never the science. The 2026-10-26 analysis next door does NOT retire this: it measures the two levers (packing x5.52, decision layer ~x3) on OTHER code, which only makes it sharper that this engine has measured neither

acts.name: Usability
acts.question: application, platform, or component?
acts.gap: nothing outside this package has ever driven a campaign; the live four-hour run on 24-25 is the reference pipeline's toolkit with an LLM on it, NOT this engine - and `--model C` with no caller falls back to model D after 5 s instead of failing

orders.name: A · full
orders.fits: 43.1 min of speech: a 50-minute slot, or a working session where questions land inline. The 2026-10-26 evidence added two slides (19 and 26) and this path grew with them

orders.name: B · default
orders.fits: 35.5 min, for a 45-minute slot: drops the loop/driver slide, the intent seam, the task-agent phases, the signature finding and the layering test. Each is recoverable in a sentence, and 5-7 still carry the map

orders.name: C · the protected core
orders.fits: 21.6 min: the protect list and nothing else. This USED to be a hard twenty; adding the lever slide and the failure-mode slide made the honest core a 25-minute path, and padding the name back down to twenty would mean cutting something the protect list says not to cut. Take a 25-minute slot, or take order C and answer questions from 20 and 25 instead of showing them

orders.name: D · for users
orders.fits: 23.6 min, for a 25-minute slot: a room that will RUN this rather than write against it. 6 carries the map for that room, so the six-surface table goes; then what a tool and a refusal are, the measured run, the lever slide (19), the four user-directed slides (22-25), and how these runs fail on a cluster (26) - which is the slide that room will actually use. No dispatcher, no protocols, no layering, no type lattice

protect: **Protect 1, 2, 3, 6, 14, 17, 18, 19, 24, 25, 26, 30, 31 and all three dividers (8, 15, 21).** Two and three are what buy the rest of the deck (the caveats at minute two and the named weak dimension); 6 is the shape of the whole system in one slide, and cutting it leaves 7 orphaned; 14 and 17 are the slides carrying evidence from a run this deck performed; 18 is what keeps the performance act honest, and 19 is the only measurement anywhere of the two levers that act's argument rests on - it is also the slide a hostile room cannot reconstruct for itself; 24, 25 and 26 carry the only evidence from real hardware and the only transcribed figures, so their red caveats travel with them or they do not travel at all; 30 is status and 31 is the asks. 20 (the interlock) is the first real content slide to go when the clock is tight - its finding fits in two sentences. Never cut a divider - a cut deck without them is a list of slides. Backups B1 (compute patterns) and B2 (the type lattice) are out of every order; do not put them back to fill time.
say_out_loud: that nothing outside this package has ever driven a campaign, so the component claim is empty and the control plane is the most carefully built unused thing in here - and the 2026-10-26 analysis next door changes NOTHING about that, because every run in it is the reference pipeline or the example next door; that the four-hour comparison on slide 24 is the REFERENCE pipeline's toolkit driven by an LLM - different code, no campaign engine, no gates, no interlock - so it is evidence about the idea and not about this engine; that both of its caveats got WORSE with the newer analysis (the reference arm's own fastrelax pass rate fell 63.6% -> 49.4% with the policy held fixed and only 1.3 of 14.2 points is binder length, and the fastrelax gap is now mostly a harness confound rather than the decision layer, since the scripted route pack-minimises 48 of 48 times and has no model in it), so nobody should quote the 3.3x; that 'agentic' predicts nothing on its own - Qwen3.5-122B gets 2.88 passing folds per GPU-hour where the scripted route gets 12.12; that packing is worth x5.52 and the decision layer about x3 and no run has ever had both, and this engine has measured NEITHER, because `replicas` IS the packing lever and has never exceeded 1 on the real chain; that of the three cluster failure modes on slide 26 this package would catch exactly one, and the one it misses is the one that looks healthiest; that `replicas > 1` DOES run - the mock campaign in this deck ran two lineages - and what has never run is `replicas > 1` on the real six-stage chain (backlog A10); and that every stage in the measured run was a mock, so the timings are the engine and never the science.
